issue.title: fix(auth): pass x-api-key header when reading Etsy user
issue.body:
## Summary

Resolves #15433

The Etsy OAuth2 adapter calls `GET https://api.etsy.com/v3/application/users/{user_id}` with only an `Authorization: Bearer` header. Etsy's v3 API requires `x-api-key: {appID}:{appSecret}` on every request. Without this header, the endpoint returns `{"error":"Invalid API key: should be in the format 'keystring:shared_secret'."}`, preventing successful profile resolution (`getUserEmail`, `getUserName`, `getUserPhoto`).

## Changes

- In `src/Appwrite/Auth/OAuth2/Etsy.php`, pass `x-api-key: {$this->appID}:{$this->appSecret}` alongside `Authorization: Bearer {$accessToken}` in `getUser()`.
- Add focused unit tests in `tests/unit/Auth/OAuth2/EtsyTest.php` covering:
  - Header injection verifying `x-api-key` and `Authorization` bearer token on Etsy user endpoint.
  - Profile attribute extraction (`getUserID`, `getUserEmail`, `getUserName`, `getUserPhoto`, `isEmailVerified`).
  - Fallback when optional user photo is missing.
  - Local caching of `$this->user` across profile getter calls.
  - PKCE login URL parameter formatting, token exchange, and refresh token exchange.

## Validation

- Code formatting checked with Pint: `passed`
- Unit tests executed with PHPUnit: `OK (8 tests, 45 assertions)`
- `git diff --check`: clean

issue.title: 🐛 Bug Report: Etsy OAuth2 adapter reads the user without the required x-api-key header

labels.name: repo-0eb169c4
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: user-6990febf/repo-c10f9604
labels.description: Fixes and upgrades for the Appwrite Auth / Users / Teams services.

issue.body:
## Summary

Sign in with Etsy still fails after #15415. After the token exchange, the adapter reads the user from Etsy's v3 API without the `x-api-key` header, which Etsy requires on every v3 request.

## Details

- `src/Appwrite/Auth/OAuth2/Etsy.php`, `getUser()`, calls `GET https://api.etsy.com/v3/application/users/{user_id}` with only an `Authorization: Bearer` header.
- Etsy requires `x-api-key: <keystring>:<shared secret>` on every v3 request: https://developers.etsy.com/documentation/essentials/requests
- Without it, the endpoint returns `{"error":"Invalid API key: should be in the format 'keystring:shared_secret'."}`, so `getUserEmail()` and `getUserName()` read keys that aren't there and sign-in fails.
- The Console already collects both values for Etsy (**Keystring** and **Shared Secret** in `src/Appwrite/Platform/Modules/Project/Http/Project/OAuth2/Etsy/Update.php`), so the adapter has them as `appID` and `appSecret`.
- The code is the same on `main` and in 2.7.1.

## Suggested fix

Send `x-api-key: {appID}:{appSecret}` with the `getUser()` request.

## Notes

- #15415 fixed the authorize URL from #15370. The adapter also still passes `scope` as an array, so the authorize URL carries `scope[0]=email_r&scope[1]=profile_r` instead of the space-separated `scope` Etsy expects. #15394, still open, fixes that part.
- This turned up while adding the held-back OAuth providers to the appwrite.io integrations catalog. The Etsy page stays held back until both are fixed.

labels.name: repo-0eb169c4
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: user-6990febf/repo-c10f9604
labels.description: Fixes and upgrades for the Appwrite Auth / Users / Teams services.

issue.body:
## Summary

The Box adapter always requests the `manage_app_users` scope. Box documents that scope as applying only to server-side (JWT) applications, so sign-in with a standard user-authentication OAuth 2.0 app is likely rejected.

## Details

- `src/Appwrite/Auth/OAuth2/Box.php` sets `$scopes = ['manage_app_users']` and sends it as `scope` on the authorize URL.
- Box's scope reference says this scope "only applies to server-side authenticated (JWT) applications": https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/scopes/
- Scopes are joined with `,`, but Box expects a space-separated list: https://developer.box.com/reference/get-authorize/
- The code is the same at HEAD and in 2.7.1.

## To confirm

I couldn't test this with a real Box app. Please confirm it with a Box OAuth 2.0 (user authentication) app before changing anything. If the scope is rejected, either omit the default scope, which makes Box fall back to the scopes configured on the app, or request `root_readonly`, and join scopes with spaces.

## Notes

This turned up while adding OAuth providers to the appwrite.io integrations catalog. The Box page is held back until this is confirmed.

issue.title: fix(oauth): remove JWT-only manage_app_users scope and space-delimit Box scopes
issue.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #15371.

1. **Remove JWT-only default scope:** Box documents `manage_app_users` as applying only to server-side authenticated (JWT) applications. Standard user authentication OAuth 2.0 apps do not use this scope and will fail authorization. The default scopes are now empty (`[]`), allowing Box to fall back to the scopes configured on the app in the Box Developer Console.
2. **Space-delimit custom scopes:** Box OAuth 2.0 requires space-delimited scopes in the authorize URL query parameter instead of comma-separated ones. Custom scopes are now joined with a space when provided, and omitted when empty.
3. **Clean token exchange parameters:** The token endpoint (`/oauth2/token`) does not take `scope` for `authorization_code` grant; removed extraneous comma-separated `scope` from token request payload.
4. **Update profile endpoint:** Point `getUser()` to Box's official `/users/me` endpoint (`https://api.box.com/2.0/users/me`).

## Test Plan

- Added unit tests in `tests/unit/Auth/OAuth2/BoxTest.php`:
  - `testDefaultScopesAreEmptyAndLoginURLOmitsScope`: verifies default scopes are empty and no `scope` param is attached to the authorize URL.
  - `testLoginURLWithCustomScopesUsesSpaceDelimiter`: verifies custom scopes are space-delimited.
  - `testTokenExchangeRequestAndResponse`: verifies token exchange payload format and headers.
  - `testRefreshTokenRequest`: verifies token refresh request.
  - `testGetUserProfileQueriesUsersMeEndpoint`: verifies user profile request to `/users/me` and attribute parsing.
- Ran test suite with PHPUnit 12.5.35:
  - `tests/unit/Auth/OAuth2/BoxTest.php`: 5 tests, 33 assertions passed.
  - Full suite `tests/unit/Auth/OAuth2/`: 99 tests, 434 assertions passed.
- Ran code formatter/linter with Pint:
  - `vendor/bin/pint --test --config pint.json src/Appwrite/Auth/OAuth2/Box.php tests/unit/Auth/OAuth2/BoxTest.php`: PASS (2 files).

## Related PRs and Issues

- Fixes #15371

issue.title: 🐛 Bug Report: Autodesk OAuth2 adapter calls retired v1 authentication endpoints

labels.name: repo-0eb169c4
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: user-6990febf/repo-c10f9604
labels.description: Fixes and upgrades for the Appwrite Auth / Users / Teams services.

issue.body:
## Summary

Sign in with Autodesk fails at the first redirect. The adapter still calls Autodesk's v1 authentication endpoints, which now return 404.

## Details

- `src/Appwrite/Auth/OAuth2/Autodesk.php` uses:
  - `https://developer.api.autodesk.com/authentication/v1/authorize`
  - `https://developer.api.autodesk.com/authentication/v1/gettoken`
  - `https://developer.api.autodesk.com/authentication/v1/refreshtoken`
- Today `v1/authorize` and `v1/gettoken` return `404`. The v2 equivalents (`/authentication/v2/authorize` and `/authentication/v2/token`) respond.
- The code is the same at HEAD and in 2.7.1.

## Suggested fix

Move the adapter to the v2 flow: https://aps.autodesk.com/en/docs/oauth/v2/developers_guide/overview/

The v2 token endpoint takes client credentials as basic auth: https://aps.autodesk.com/en/docs/oauth/v2/reference/http/gettoken-POST/

The user profile call (`userprofile/v1/users/@me`) is worth checking at the same time.

## Notes

This turned up while adding OAuth providers to the appwrite.io integrations catalog. The Autodesk page is held back until this is fixed.

issue.title: 🐛 Bug Report: Stripe OAuth2 sign-in fails because the token exchange never sends the secret key

labels.name: repo-0eb169c4
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: user-6990febf/repo-c10f9604
labels.description: Fixes and upgrades for the Appwrite Auth / Users / Teams services.

issue.body:
## Summary

Sign in with Stripe can't complete. `Appwrite\Auth\OAuth2\Stripe::getTokens()` posts the authorization code to `https://connect.stripe.com/oauth/token` without authenticating, so Stripe rejects the code exchange. The **API Secret Key** saved in the provider settings is never sent.

## Details

- `src/Appwrite/Auth/OAuth2/Stripe.php`, `getTokens()`: the body contains only `grant_type` and `code`, and the headers array is empty.
- `refreshTokens()` has the same gap.
- Stripe requires the platform's secret key on this request, sent as the basic-auth user or bearer token: https://docs.stripe.com/connect/oauth-reference
- The code is the same at HEAD and in 2.7.1.

## Suggested fix

Authenticate the token and refresh requests with the stored secret key, for example `Authorization: Bearer <secret key>`.

## Notes

This comes from reading the adapter against Stripe's OAuth reference. I didn't reproduce it with live Stripe credentials. It turned up while adding OAuth providers to the appwrite.io integrations catalog, and the Stripe catalog page is held back until this is fixed.

cc @adityaoberai

issue.title: 🐛 Bug Report: Turning off Public when creating a function from a template still lets anyone execute it

labels.name: repo-0eb169c4
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: user-6990febf/repo-64e7300b
labels.description: Fixes and upgrades for the Appwrite Functions.

issue.body:
## Summary

When you create a function from a template in the Console, turning off the **Public** switch ("Allow anyone to execute this function (execute role: any)") has no effect. The function is still created with `execute: ['any']`, so anyone who finds its domain can run it.

## Details

- `apps/console/src/components/pages/projects/$projectId/functions/create/TemplateConfigView.tsx`, around line 300, builds the execute permissions as `isPublic ? ['any'] : template.permissions?.length ? template.permissions : []`.
- Every function template in `app/config/templates/function.php` sets `'permissions' => ['any']`, so the "off" branch also resolves to `['any']`.
- The manual, repository and URL flows (`ManualCreateView.tsx`, `RepositoryConfigView.tsx` and `DeployFromUrlView.tsx`) send `[]` when the switch is off, so only the template flow is affected.
- The code is the same at HEAD and in 2.7.1.

## Suggested fix

Send exactly what the switch shows: `['any']` when it's on and `[]` when it's off. If a template should start private, set the switch's initial state from the template's permissions instead.

## Notes

This comes from reading the Console code. I didn't reproduce it in a running Console. It turned up while writing the appwrite.io integrations catalog pages in #15374, which tell readers to change execute access after creating these template functions.

cc @adityaoberai

issue.title: fix(console): keep full-screen curtains clickable over an open dialog
issue.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the password breach curtain's buttons doing nothing when clicked.

A modal dialog, such as the GitHub star prompt, turns off pointer events on the page body while it's open. The full-screen curtain shows on top of it, but it inherited that setting, so **Update password** and **Remind me later** ignored clicks. The curtain now sets `pointer-events-auto`, so it always takes clicks. This applies to every full-screen curtain (password breach, project blocks, offline state), since they share `FullScreenCurtain`.

issue.title: fix(console): domain status, apex records, claim and SMTP fixes
issue.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the remaining Console bugs in custom domains.

**Organization domains**
- The nameserver state moves from **Status** to the **Nameservers** field: "Appwrite" in green, or "3rd party" in yellow. The banner above keeps its Retry Verification button. Status shows only while a transfer is in progress, since a status should show progress.

**Adding a domain**
- Apex domains show A/AAAA records, never a CNAME on `@`, which registrars can't accept at the apex.
- The claim step explains why it's needed: the domain is used by another project, and verifying moves it here.
- The SMTP wizard has the claim step too. Before, moving an email domain between projects stopped at a claim error with no way forward.
- An empty CAA target no longer shows as a blank CAA record.

**Verify and Retry**
- Retry no longer waits on the nameserver check, which runs an external lookup it doesn't need.
- The badge shows when a certificate is blocked waiting on a DNS record, and tells the user to add it.
- After a verify, the domain lists on function deployment pages refresh too.

**Delete**
- The Delete confirmation names the domain.

**Other**
- Hebrew and Japanese strings for the new text.
- Unit tests no longer leak module mocks into other files: tests restore from a copy of the real module.

## Test Plan

- Added unit tests:
  - `domain-rule-dialogs`
  - `organization-domain-status`
  - `smtp-domain-claim`
  - more cases in `proxy-domain-records`, `proxy-rule-status` and `verify-domain-cname`
- Full Console unit suite: 1056 pass, 0 fail.
- ESLint and Prettier are clean on the changed files.
- I reproduced on prod, with a real domain, the bugs this fixes: the "Appwrite DNS" status, the claim text, an unnamed Delete, and CNAME on `@` for an apex.

## Related PRs and Issues

- Follows #15332 and #15365.

- [x] Have you read the [Contributing Guidelines on issues](https://github.com/appwrite/appwrite/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)?

issue.title: fix: faster domain verification and certificate renewal fixes
issue.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the server bugs behind expired custom domain certificates and slow domain verification.

**Certificates**
- A certificate that expired in the last 30 days is still checked. Before, once a certificate reached 5 attempts it dropped out of every check after expiry and kept serving the expired certificate, with no alert.
- A rule isn't reported as verified while the first certificate it inherited is expired.
- A blocked certificate is logged as waiting while attempts remain, not as failed.

**Verification**
- A rule's DNS checks (CNAME, A, AAAA, CAA) run in parallel with a 3 s timeout. Before, they ran one after another at 5 s each with no overall cap, so adding or retrying an apex domain could take 40 s or more.
- The failure reason names the record type and the resolver, instead of just "DNS query failed".

**CAA**
- An empty CAA target comes back as an empty string. Before, every default self-hosted install recommended `CAA 0 issue ""`, which blocks every CA for the whole domain.

## Test Plan

- Unit test in `packages/dns`: a failed query names the record type and the resolver.
- E2E: `ConsoleConsoleClientTest` checks the CAA variable is never `0 issue ""`.
- `php -l` is clean on every changed file. Pint, PHPStan and Rector run in CI.

## Related PRs and Issues

- Console side: #15366.

issue.body:
### 👟 Reproduction steps

Using Console only:

1. Open Databases → a TablesDB table with optional integer `quantity` and float `price` columns, with no defaults or bounds excluding zero.
2. Click **Create row** and enter `0` in either field. The input immediately clears to `NULL`.
3. Click **Create row**. The resulting row contains `null`, rather than `0`.
4. Repeat using an existing row's **Actions → Update** form: entering zero also clears the field, and Update saves null.
5. As controls, positive and negative values work in the form. Double-clicking a numeric cell, entering `0`, and committing the inline edit also saves zero correctly.

### 👍 Expected behavior

An explicitly entered `0` should remain numeric zero. Clearing an optional field may produce null; zero should not be treated as an empty field.

### 👎 Actual Behavior

Create/Update forms convert zero to null and report a successful save. Users cannot record values such as zero inventory or a zero price through these forms.

The scalar numeric handlers use `parseInt(value, 10) || null` / `parseFloat(value) || null`, so valid zero falls through to null:

- [TablesDB form](https://github.com/appwrite/appwrite/blob/89244fb8026ca845f24ade6e418833e0c2bfb2e6/apps/console/src/components/pages/projects/%24projectId/databases/tablesdb/Spreadsheet.tsx#L2058)

These two paths are code-confirmed; browser reproduction was TablesDB.

Existing [numeric-field tests](https://github.com/appwrite/appwrite/blob/89244fb8026ca845f24ade6e418833e0c2bfb2e6/apps/console/tests/unit/numeric-field.test.ts#L14) explicitly preserve a typed zero.

Self-hosted Appwrite 2.6.2, Console `appwrite/new:1.1.180-self-hosted`, Docker Compose with PostgreSQL. Reproduced in the Console browser UI. Affected handlers also checked on current main.

labels.name: user-ce4cd42c/repo-550db293
labels.description: Fixes and upgrades for the Appwrite CLI.

issue.body:
Tracks PR #14497.

## Plan

**Goal:** Keep `project.updateOAuth2Kakao` in its released SDK parameter order (`clientId, clientSecret, prompt, enabled`). #14467 moved `prompt` after `enabled` for every provider on the OAuth2 `Base` path, so the next SDK regeneration would shift existing positional Kakao calls.

**What changes:**
- `src/Appwrite/Platform/Modules/Project/Http/Project/OAuth2/Base.php`: new `isPromptBeforeEnabled()` hook (defaults to `false`). When a provider returns `true`, `prompt` is declared before `enabled` and the route uses a new `updateWithPromptFirst()` callback that forwards to `updateWithPrompt()` with the arguments in the right order.
- `src/Appwrite/Platform/Modules/Project/Http/Project/OAuth2/Kakao/Update.php`: overrides `isPromptBeforeEnabled()` to return `true`.
- `app/config/sdks/parameters.lock.json`: both `project.updateOAuth2Kakao` entries record `prompt` before `enabled`.
- Other providers keep their current order: Discord, GitHub and Zoho stay `clientId, clientSecret, enabled, prompt`, and Amazon (no prompt) stays `clientId, clientSecret, enabled`.

**Remaining steps:** None. The linked PR is the full change.

**Done when:**
- [ ] `tests/unit/SDK/ParametersTest.php` passes against the updated lock
- [ ] Kakao's declared params and callback arguments are both `clientId, clientSecret, prompt, enabled`

labels.name: user-ce4cd42c/repo-550db293
labels.description: Fixes and upgrades for the Appwrite CLI.

issue.body:
### 👟 Reproduction steps

1. Self-hosted Appwrite 2.3.0 with `_APP_EMAIL_CERTIFICATES` and `_APP_SYSTEM_SECURITY_EMAIL_ADDRESS` empty (e.g. TLS terminated by a reverse proxy, so no Let's Encrypt is needed).
2. Create a bucket and upload a few files.
3. Delete the bucket (`DELETE /v1/storage/buckets/{bucketId}` → `204`).
4. Look at the uploads volume and at the deletes queue.

### 👍 Expected behavior

The deletes worker removes the bucket's files (and performs all other cleanup jobs) – a certificate email should only be needed when a certificate is actually issued.

### 👎 Actual Behavior

- The files stay on disk (50 of 50 files and the bucket directory still present 90 s after the deletion, two runs).
- The job ends up in `utopia-queue.failed.v1-deletes`; the worker logs for it:
  ```
  Exception: You must set a valid security email address (_APP_EMAIL_CERTIFICATES) to issue a LetsEncrypt SSL certificate.
    at /usr/src/code/app/worker.php:43
  ```

Cause: the deletes worker injects the `certificates` resource for every job ([`Workers/Deletes.php` L70](https://github.com/appwrite/appwrite/blob/2.3.0/src/Appwrite/Platform/Workers/Deletes.php#L70)), and that resource throws while it is being created when no email is set ([`app/worker.php`](https://github.com/appwrite/appwrite/blob/2.3.0/app/worker.php)). Because resources are resolved before the action runs, **every** job of the deletes worker fails this way – not only certificate-related ones (bucket files, and per the code also project/user/session cleanup, execution and audit retention, deployments, cache). Nothing in the console or the API shows that the cleanup failed. `main` has the same resource definition.

### 🎲 Appwrite version

2.3.0

### 💻 Operating system

Linux (Debian 12), Docker

### 🧱 Your Environment

Self-hosted Appwrite 2.3.0 behind a reverse proxy, `_APP_STORAGE_DEVICE=local`, two API nodes.

### 💡 Suggested fix

Create the Let's Encrypt client lazily (only where a certificate is issued or revoked) or let the resource return `null` and fail only the certificate code path. Additionally, the installer/health check could warn when the variable is empty.

issue.title: 🐛 Bug Report: Webhook destination check runs after the TCP connect, so webhook logs reveal internal hosts and ports

labels.name: user-6990febf/repo-29b64d5b
labels.description: Fixes and upgrades for the Appwrite Database.

labels.name: user-6990febf/repo-16afa850
labels.description: Fixes and upgrades for the Appwrite Messaging.

labels.name: user-6990febf/repo-9cecfe6a
labels.description: Fixes and upgrades for the Appwrite Domains.

labels.name: user-6990febf/repo-27f9ff75
labels.description: Fixes and upgrades for Appwrite Sites.

labels.name: user-ce4cd42c/repo-550db293
labels.description: Fixes and upgrades for the Appwrite CLI.

issue.body:
### 👟 Reproduction steps

Webhooks on `rows.*.create`, one row created, then `GET /v1/projects/{id}/webhooks/{id}` → `logs`:

| URL | Log |
|---|---|
| `http://<docker-ip-dashed>.sslip.io:18099/` (port open) | `Connection to 172.18.0.21 refused: not an allowed destination.` |
| same host, port 18098 (closed) | `Failed to connect to … after 31 ms: Could not connect to server` |
| `http://10-255-255-1.sslip.io/` (no host) | `Connection timed out after 15000 milliseconds` |

2 of 2 runs identical. No HTTP request reaches the target (verified with a listener), but the TCP handshake does.

### 👍 Expected behavior

Webhooks to private addresses are rejected before any connection is made, and the webhook logs do not reveal whether an internal host or port is reachable.

### 👎 Actual Behavior

Webhook delivery to private addresses is blocked by `PublicInternet`, but the check runs **after** the TCP connection is established (`CURLOPT_PREREQFUNCTION`). The error stored in the webhook's `logs` therefore reveals the state of any internal host/port reachable from the webhooks worker. A project member who can create webhooks can use a DNS name that resolves to a private address (e.g. `172-18-0-21.sslip.io`) – such URLs pass validation at creation – to scan the internal network.

`packages/client/src/Adapter/Curl/Client.php` in the 2.4.0 tag: the allowed-destination check is done in `CURLOPT_PREREQFUNCTION` (L387–L399), i.e. after the connection is established; the error text is built at L256 and stored in the webhook `logs`.

**Impact:** Internal port and host discovery (Docker networks, VPN ranges such as 100.64.0.0/10, cloud metadata reachability) from the worker's network position; on multi-tenant installations any user who can create a project. Data is not sent.

### 🎲 Appwrite version

2.4.0 (measured); earlier versions not tested

### 💻 Operating system

Linux (Debian 12), Docker

### 🧱 Your Environment

Self-hosted, webhooks worker on a Docker network with other services; default `_APP_ALLOWED_INTERNAL_ADDRESSES`.

### 💡 Suggested fix

Resolve the hostname first and check every resolved address against the destinations before connecting (`CURLOPT_RESOLVE` / `CURLOPT_OPENSOCKETFUNCTION`, or connect only to the pre-validated IP), and/or store a uniform error ("destination not allowed or unreachable") in the webhook logs. Optionally reject URLs whose host resolves to a private address at creation.

**Proposed severity:** Low–Medium, CWE-204 (related CWE-918), CVSS 3.1 `AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:N/A:N` (4.3).

### 👀 Have you spent some time to check if this issue has been raised before?

- [x] I checked and didn't find a similar issue

### 🏢 Have you read the Code of Conduct?

issue.body:
### 👟 Reproduction steps

Webhooks on `rows.*.create`, one row created, then `GET /v1/projects/{id}/webhooks/{id}` → `logs`:

| URL | Log |
|---|---|
| `http://<docker-ip-dashed>.sslip.io:18099/` (port open) | `Connection to 172.18.0.21 refused: not an allowed destination.` |
| same host, port 18098 (closed) | `Failed to connect to … after 31 ms: Could not connect to server` |
| `http://10-255-255-1.sslip.io/` (no host) | `Connection timed out after 15000 milliseconds` |

2 of 2 runs identical. No HTTP request reaches the target (verified with a listener), but the TCP handshake does.

### 👍 Expected behavior

Webhooks to private addresses are rejected before any connection is made, and the webhook logs do not reveal whether an internal host or port is reachable.

### 👎 Actual Behavior

Webhook delivery to private addresses is blocked by `PublicInternet`, but the check runs **after** the TCP connection is established (`CURLOPT_PREREQFUNCTION`). The error stored in the webhook's `logs` therefore reveals the state of any internal host/port reachable from the webhooks worker. A project member who can create webhooks can use a DNS name that resolves to a private address (e.g. `172-18-0-21.sslip.io`) – such URLs pass validation at creation – to scan the internal network.

`packages/client/src/Adapter/Curl/Client.php` in the 2.4.0 tag: the allowed-destination check is done in `CURLOPT_PREREQFUNCTION` (L387–L399), i.e. after the connection is established; the error text is built at L256 and stored in the webhook `logs`.

**Impact:** Internal port and host discovery (Docker networks, VPN ranges such as 100.64.0.0/10, cloud metadata reachability) from the worker's network position; on multi-tenant installations any user who can create a project. Data is not sent.

### 🎲 Appwrite version

2.4.0 (measured); earlier versions not tested

### 💻 Operating system

Linux (Debian 12), Docker

### 🧱 Your Environment

Self-hosted, webhooks worker on a Docker network with other services; default `_APP_ALLOWED_INTERNAL_ADDRESSES`.

### 💡 Suggested fix

Resolve the hostname first and check every resolved address against the destinations before connecting (`CURLOPT_RESOLVE` / `CURLOPT_OPENSOCKETFUNCTION`, or connect only to the pre-validated IP), and/or store a uniform error ("destination not allowed or unreachable") in the webhook logs. Optionally reject URLs whose host resolves to a private address at creation.

**Proposed severity:** Low–Medium, CWE-204 (related CWE-918), CVSS 3.1 `AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:N/A:N` (4.3).

   ```json
   }
   ```

2. Accept the invitation using `PATCH /v1/teams/<TEAM_ID>/memberships/<MEMBERSHIP_ID>/status` with the returned `userId` and invitation-link `secret`. Confirm the membership is active and the user's email is verified. Setting a password and signing in again also reproduces this.

   ```json
   {
     "messageId": "unique()",
     "subject": "Invitation messaging test",
     "content": "Test message",
     "users": ["<USER_ID>"]
   }
   ```

issue.body:
### 👟 Reproduction steps

1. Create a user with a verified email and enable MFA (`mfa: true`, an authenticator added).
2. Log in with email and password only: `POST /v1/account/sessions/email` → session with `factors: ["password"]`.
3. With this session, `GET /v1/account` and `GET` a row readable only by `user:<id>`.
4. Open `wss://<host>/v1/realtime?project=<id>` with the same session cookie and subscribe to a table channel and to `account`.
5. Create a row with `read("user:<id>")` (e.g. with an API key).

### 👍 Expected behavior

Realtime rejects the session the same way the HTTP API does (`user_more_factors_required`) until the second factor is completed. No user data and no events are delivered.

### 👎 Actual Behavior

| Step | Response |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/account` | `401 user_more_factors_required` (correct) |
| `GET` row with `read(user:<id>)` | `401` (correct) |
| Realtime connect | accepted; the `connected` message contains the complete user document (email, targets, prefs, `mfa`, …) |
| Subscribe to table channel and `account` | accepted |
| Row created with `read(user:<id>)` | event with the full row data delivered to this connection |

Two runs, on both realtime nodes, identical. Someone who knows the password but not the second factor can read live everything the account can read through realtime: rows, file metadata, account, team and membership events. MFA is not enforced for realtime at all.

Cause: the HTTP API checks the factors in [`app/controllers/shared/api.php` L545–L564](https://github.com/appwrite/appwrite/blob/2.4.0/app/controllers/shared/api.php#L545-L564). `app/realtime.php` resolves the user and roles from the session on connect and in the `authentication` message handler, but never looks at `mfa`, the user's verified factors or `session.factors`. The password-reset check that comes before it in `shared/api.php` is missing too (from the code, not measured). 2.3.0 behaves the same.

### 🎲 Appwrite version

2.4.0 (also 2.3.0)

### 💻 Operating system

Linux (Debian 12), Docker

### 🧱 Your Environment

Self-hosted Appwrite 2.4.0, two API nodes, two realtime nodes.

### 💡 Suggested fix

Apply the same factor check (and the password-reset check) in realtime on connect, on the `authentication` message and whenever roles are recomputed; reject with `user_more_factors_required`.

### 👀 Have you spent some time to check if this issue has been raised before?

- [x] I checked and didn't find a similar issue

### 🏢 Have you read the Code of Conduct?

- [x] I have read the Code of Conduct

Related: #14415 (plaintext `secret` in server-side token/session events) makes this worse. If a backend creates tokens or sessions for the user through the server API, those secrets reach the `account` channel in clear text, which turns this read bypass into a full account takeover.
